Estimate total study cost

Source: R/estimate_cost.R
estimate_cost.Rd

Costs an MMS study from its design choices, as a cost for each stage a sample passes through plus a per-site cost:

  • Stage costs: for each of up to three stages, the number of people or samples reaching that stage times that stage's cost per person or sample. The stages are:

    screened

    people screened for infection at enrolment: consent, interview, a rapid test or microscopy.

    collected

    people a sample is collected from: a dried blood spot or blood draw, storage and shipping.

    sequenced

    samples taken through the molecular laboratory: extraction, PCR or sequencing, data management.

  • Site cost = the sum over sites of (fixed cost per site + transport cost per site). The fixed cost (training, equipment, administration) and the transport cost may each be given once for all sites or as one value per site.

The stages are nested: everyone collected was first screened, and every sample sequenced was first collected. So n_collected is a subset of n_screened, not in addition to it (for example, only those who test positive), and n_sequenced is a subset of n_collected (for example, after lost or failed samples). A person is counted at every stage they reach, and each stage's cost is the cost of that stage alone, not of everything up to it. Give only the stages a study has; at least one is needed. A study costed with a single all-in cost per sample can give that as n_sequenced and cost_per_sequenced.

Pairs with the design functions: their $n is the number of samples needed at analysis, so it is n_sequenced; scale it up for losses and for suspected cases that turn out negative to get n_collected and n_screened. Take n_sites from the design function's result too. To cost several regions, call estimate_cost() once per region and add the totals. All monetary inputs and outputs are in one currency unit.

Usage

estimate_cost(
  n_screened = NULL,
  cost_per_screened = NULL,
  n_collected = NULL,
  cost_per_collected = NULL,
  n_sequenced = NULL,
  cost_per_sequenced = NULL,
  n_sites = NULL,
  fixed_cost_per_site = 0,
  transport_cost_per_site = 0,
  budget = NULL
)

Arguments

n_screened, n_collected, n_sequenced

Optional whole numbers. The number of people or samples reaching each stage (see Description). Each is no larger than the one before it. For n_sequenced, $n from any design function (for design_difference(), the total across both groups).

cost_per_screened, cost_per_collected, cost_per_sequenced

Non-negative numbers. The cost of each stage per person or sample reaching it. Give each one with its n_ argument, or neither.

n_sites

Optional whole number. Total number of sites to cost: $n_sites from a design function (for design_difference(), sum(n_sites)). NULL (default) costs the stages only.

fixed_cost_per_site

Non-negative fixed cost per site: one number for every site, or one value per site (length n_sites). Default 0.

transport_cost_per_site

Non-negative transport cost per site: one number for every site, or one value per site. Default 0.

budget

Optional positive number. Total money available.

Value

A list with:

total_cost

variable_cost + site_cost.

variable_cost

The sum of stage_cost.

stage_cost

Named vector of the cost of each stage (screened, collected, sequenced): its number times its cost, or 0 for a stage not given.

site_cost

Sum over sites of fixed plus transport cost; 0 when n_sites is NULL.

budget_remaining

budget - total_cost (negative if over budget), or NULL when no budget is given.

References

MMS-SD Study Design Workshop, budget-officer activity; Modules 2 and 7. https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMS-SD_workshop/

Examples

# One all-in cost per sample
estimate_cost(n_sequenced = 323, cost_per_sequenced = 50)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 16150
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 16150
#> 
#> $stage_cost
#>  screened collected sequenced 
#>         0         0     16150 
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#> 

# Three stages: 1,950 screened, the 780 positives sampled, 700 sequenced
# after losses; 12 sites at 5,000 fixed + 1,000 transport each
estimate_cost(n_screened  = 1950, cost_per_screened  = 2,
              n_collected = 780,  cost_per_collected = 15,
              n_sequenced = 700,  cost_per_sequenced = 40,
              n_sites = 12, fixed_cost_per_site = 5000,
              transport_cost_per_site = 1000)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 115600
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 43600
#> 
#> $stage_cost
#>  screened collected sequenced 
#>      3900     11700     28000 
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 72000
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#> 

# A different fixed cost at each of 3 sites, checked against a budget
estimate_cost(n_sequenced = 50, cost_per_sequenced = 10, n_sites = 3,
              fixed_cost_per_site = c(100, 200, 300), budget = 1500)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 1100
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 500
#> 
#> $stage_cost
#>  screened collected sequenced 
#>         0         0       500 
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 600
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> [1] 400
#> 

# Cost a design, allowing 10% of samples to be lost and 40% of suspected
# cases to be positive
des <- design_precision(prevalence = 0.15, moe = 0.05, n_per_site = 30, icc = 0.05)
n_collected <- ceiling(des$n / 0.9)
estimate_cost(n_screened  = ceiling(n_collected / 0.4), cost_per_screened  = 2,
              n_collected = n_collected,                cost_per_collected = 15,
              n_sequenced = des$n,                      cost_per_sequenced = 40,
              n_sites = des$n_sites, fixed_cost_per_site = 5000,
              transport_cost_per_site = 1200)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 145200
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 33600
#> 
#> $stage_cost
#>  screened collected sequenced 
#>      3000      9000     21600 
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 111600
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#> 

# Cost a two-group design: design_difference() gives one n_sites per
# group, so add them up
des2 <- design_difference(0.10, 0.20, n_per_site1 = 30, icc = 0.05)
estimate_cost(n_sequenced = des2$n, cost_per_sequenced = 50,
              n_sites = sum(des2$n_sites), fixed_cost_per_site = 5000)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 221000
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 51000
#> 
#> $stage_cost
#>  screened collected sequenced 
#>         0         0     51000 
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 170000
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#>
